body.x: AVING News selected ▲Intel’s “Adrenaline Dress”, ▲MISFIT’s “Ray”, ▲Sensoria’s “Smart Socks”, ▲ZEISS’ “Smart Glasses”, and ▲LOGBAR’s “Ili” as the top five products among wearable devices showcased at “CES (Consumer Technology Show) 2016”, the world’s largest IT consumer electronics exhibition, which runs for four days from Wednesday the 6th to Saturday the 9th in Las Vegas.

The “Adrenaline Dress” makes use of Intel’s Curie Module, a low-power solution for wearable devices. It detects various changes, including one’s adrenaline, body temperature, breathing, perspiration, and stress, all according to one’s physical condition. Then a carbon-fiber lattice extends and changes the design of the dress.

“Ray” attracts much attention with its unique cylinder-shaped design, which goes beyond the designs of general watches. It tracks activity and sleep by using a 3-axis accelerometer and is equipped with a vibration motor that can sense subtle motions. Furthermore, it can receive calls when it is connected to a smartphone. And it provides text and mail notifications via vibrations.

On the upper part of “Smart Socks” are five magnetic studs, and they collect and record users’ levels of activity. Three sensors on the lower part of the socks record and analyze the location of feet and users’ weight and gait.

Unlike the designs of existing smart glasses, “Smart Glasses” looks just like normal glasses. It is compatible with general frames by using ZEISS’ curved smart lens technology, which puts data directly inside the glasses. Frames made by general glasses manufacturers can also be used.

“Ili” is a portable necklace-type translator. It can translate up to 50,000 words and sentences without Internet connection. It provides accurate translations, even in noisy environments. Currently, it is providing translation services for English, Chinese, and Japanese, and will support other various languages, including Korean and French.

“CES”, which is held every year in January by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is the world’s largest IT consumer electronics exhibition, showcasing global trends in the electronics and IT industry. AVING News, which has sent reporters to CES for 11 years, will introduce various up-to-date technologies and products showcased at CES 2016.
